headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create default data-leak and prompt-injection risk; Semantic Kernel can also amplify Kotaemon outputs into downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kotaemon reads and writes ./ktem_app_data and handles HTML/MHTML/PDFs, while Semantic Kernel has MCP/plugin-based tool use and application-defined files. That creates a plausible shared-content bridge where attacker-controlled content from A can be treated as instructions by B. No direct provenance controls are shown, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or memory-backed content store
IF B ingests A-produced HTML/PDF/chat output as prompt text or plugin input
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces
Disable automatic ingestion of A outputs into B prompts
Add provenance tags to all shared documents
Review MCP/plugin inputs before execution
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping filters

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kotaemon touches API keys and broad document types, and Semantic Kernel has broad network egress plus read/write filesystem access. If they share a workspace or application context, sensitive files from A can flow into B and then out through B's API calls. The pairwise leakage pathway is default-plausible and the blast radius includes secrets and documents.
conditions: IF A stores documents or API keys in ./ktem_app_data
IF B is given access to the same directory or shared memory store
IF B forwards loaded context to external model providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Put each agent in a separate OS user or container
Remove secrets from any shared workspace
Restrict B's outbound network destinations
Rotate any API keys exposed to A
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kotaemon supports multiple instances and writes to ./ktem_app_data, while Semantic Kernel supports multiple instances with shared state via memory stores and can write files. Even without shell access, overlapping writes to shared mutable resources can race or overwrite each other's artifacts. The profiles do not show locking, so conflict is plausible in default multi-instance deployments.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or memory store
IF multiple instances run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint storage paths
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Turn off shared-state features for one agent
Check for file-lock support before concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency or locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Semantic Kernel is a library for agents/plugins, so it can treat upstream outputs as prompt or tool input. Kotaemon produces document-grounded answers and citations, which B may relay into plugins or model calls without verification. That makes A's mistakes or prompt injections cascade into B's downstream actions, and the profiles do not show a mandatory verification gate.
conditions: IF B uses A's answers as authoritative context
IF B triggers plugins or OpenAPI tools from A-generated text without validation
mitigations: Require human review before tool execution
Add a verification step for all A-derived claims
Limit B to read-only actions
Log source provenance for every forwarded fact
requires-engineering: implement claim-checking against original documents

E_compliance.rationale: Kotaemon handles chat transcripts, documents, and API keys, while Semantic Kernel handles application context and plugin credentials. If the same regulated data class is routed through both, differing retention or residency policies can create a compliance mismatch. The profiles do not document aligned controls, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated documents or chat transcripts are shared between the agents
IF one agent retains or logs data longer than the other
IF either agent routes EU or PHI data to a non-approved backend
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent
Disable retention on shared transcripts where possible
Keep regulated data out of external model calls
Document residency and retention settings for both agents
requires-engineering: align compliance controls and DPA terms
